messages:
elaine: Heads-up: dashboards are showing a big perf regression after the midnight deploy. Charts take ~2.5s to first-draw now (was ~600ms). Screenshot + flame in trace: https://img.redwood/snap/abc123.png

 dave: ugh, saw this too. Is it specific to heatmaps or all charts?

 elaine: Looks worst for multi-series heatmaps and the metric-grid. Also noticed main bundle size jump + parse time up ~30%.

 priya: any telemetry traces? can we see where the time is spent (parse vs render vs GC)?

 ben: CI perf traces show a spike in main-thread parse + long tasks around 3.1s. flame points at telem-init (telemetry client) + new i18n chunk.

 nina: telemetry client was rolled with eager-init change in canary - it now preloads locale bundles synchronously. I filed PR #2378.

 elaine: that aligns. If telemetry is blocking parse, we can revert eager-init. Who owns the rollout?

 priya: that was me. I added eager-init to get more consistent metrics for the new routing policy rollout. Didn't expect it to inflate parse time this much.

 ben: quick mitigation: lazy-load telemetry again but keep a tiny sync hook for critical tags. Something like:
```
// telemetry bootstrap
if (window.REDWOOD_FAST_METRICS) {
  import('./telem-boot').then(init);
} else {
  // defer to idle
  requestIdleCallback(()=>import('./telem-boot').then(init));
}
```

 dave: also noticed KV cache key TTL change in the backend routing layer yesterday — could be increasing payload sizes for chart endpoints? Any correlation in network size?

 elaine: payloads for /metrics/series are same, but bundle bytes delivered to client are +250kb on first load (source-map stripped).

 nina: the i18n chunk bump + a new shared-embedlib export got bundled into main because of a rollup change. Rollup config was tweaked in #2360. I'll revert that chunk split change.

 priya: can we backfill a quick canary: revert eager telemetry + revert rollup tweak on canary channel, run perf harness? If that brings LCP back, we know it's frontend bundling.

 ben: yes. I can cut a canary at 12:30. CI perf job (perf-runner) will run the dashboard harness and upload traces to perf-trace.

 ci-bot: Deploy queued: canary/deploy-1758901234-revert-eager-telem at 2025-03-11T12:30:00Z.

 dave: small thing — routing-policy change also changed cache-control headers for chunk responses (shorter TTL). That increases revalidation on client; if browsers re-fetch, it adds parse overhead. Anyone touch asset headers?

 nina: that was in the same PR as KV TTL. I'll set Cache-Control to previous values for JS chunks in the canary.

 elaine: after canary is live, pls ping with perf numbers. If good, we should hotfix the main release and also add a gated perf check to the rollout job so eager-init can't land without a perf baseline.

 priya: agreed. I'll add a perf-blocker label and stop the rollout until we have a pass. Also will add a small synthetic LCP check in the PR job (headless-run + threshold).

 ben: postmortem actions: 1) revert eager telemetry init; 2) revert rollup chunking tweak; 3) revert chunk header TTL change; 4) add perf gate to rollout PRs. Can we scope owners for each?

 nina: I'll take (2) and (3).

 priya: I'll take (1) and add the perf gate.

 dave: I'll own validating the network traces and verifying payload sizes.

 elaine: thanks. If canary shows <800ms first-draw, cut a production hotfix.

 ci-bot: Canary deploy succeeded: canary/deploy-1758901234-revert-eager-telem at 2025-03-11T12:37:10Z. Perf job started: https://ci.redwood/perf/1758901234

 ben: perf job finished — dashboard LCP median 680ms, main parse time back down to 640ms. Looks like the two reverts fixed it.

 priya: great. I'll open hotfix PR to main and tag for immediate rollout. Also will add a PR check that runs the synthetic LCP and blocks merge if >1s regressions.

 nina: note to self: audit rollup changes for accidental main-bundle imports. We should add a bundle-size lint check in CI too.

 elaine: good work team. Let's still follow up with a short postmortem summarizing cause + remediation and add to our rollout playbook.

 dave: 👍
